name: pvlib-python-spectral-grid-semantics-and-386c
instr:
Give pvlib a common wavelength-aware representation so spectra can move through reference, atmospheric, system, and simulation workflows without callers reshaping or interpolating them. Spectral transfer must conserve physical energy, expose incomplete coverage, and respect wavelength units. Existing pandas behavior and legacy entry points must remain compatible.

`pvlib.spectrum` publicly exports `SpectralAxis`, `SpectralAxisError`, `SpectralData`, `ResamplingReport`, `SpectralCoverageError`, `conservative_resample`, `SpectralComponents`, `get_reference_spectra`, `average_photon_energy`, `sr_to_qe`, `qe_to_sr`, `calc_spectral_mismatch_field`, and `spectrl2`. Valid axes represent finite, positive, strictly increasing wavelengths in nm, um, or m, preserve explicit edges through `from_centers` and `to`, and reject invalid coordinates with `SpectralAxisError`, a `ValueError`. Spectral data preserves its declared wavelength orientation, component identity, and pandas labels through `from_pandas` and `to_pandas`. Conservative overlap transfer preserves covered integrated energy and reports both omitted bands, raising `SpectralCoverageError`, a `ValueError`, when strict coverage is required. Photon-energy integration, response conversion, and three-grid mismatch calculations use physical coordinates; `sr_to_qe` and `qe_to_sr` are reversible without normalization, while `calc_spectral_mismatch_field` rejects inadequate strict coverage. `spectrl2` can expose every irradiance componen
